info.title: Tessaro device API
info.description: The API of one Tessaro device, over HTTPS on port 7400 with the device's own self-signed certificate: pin its SHA-256 fingerprint (`/api/v1/device/id`, the mDNS `fp` record). An unclaimed device answers everything without a token; once claimed, everything but identification, the claim and signing in needs `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, or a Webconfig browser session's cookie.

oneOf.description: 400: the query or the body is not what the endpoint takes.
401: the device is claimed and this needs a token.
401: the token is not one of the device's.
404: no such endpoint, or no such job.
413: the body is too large.
422: the device refused: `error` says why.
429: too many invalid tokens from this address; wait a minute.
500: the device failed to answer.

403: a browser request from another site, or a browser write with
the wrong content type.

id.description: The app-specific id derived from /etc/machine-id. Never the machine id.

fingerprint.description: SHA-256 of the device's TLS certificate, lower-case hex.

os.description:
`PRETTY_NAME` and `IMAGE_VERSION` from the image's os-release, so an
update can be seen to have landed. Defaulted for older devices.

maintenance.description:
In maintenance mode `kiosk_url` is the maintenance page's. Defaulted,
so a client still reads an agent that predates it.

debug_screen.description:
The debug screen is up, whatever `kiosk_url` says. Defaulted the same
way.

devtools.description:
A DevTools client other than the agent is connected to the browser,
so the agent leaves the tab alone (docs/kiosk-browser.md). Defaulted
the same way.

audio.description:
Where sound plays and at what volume. `None` from a device that
predates audio.

data.description: How full `/data` is. Defaulted the same way.

screen_on.description: Whether the display is on; `None` when the compositor cannot say.

bridge.description:
The page bridge: `browser.bridge.mode`, and the injected script with
its state. Defaulted the same way.

time.description: The timezone and whether the clock is in sync. Defaulted the same way.

hardware.description: Vendor, model, board and CPU. Defaulted the same way.

memory.description: How much RAM there is and how much is in use. Defaulted the same way.

cpu_percent.description:
How busy the CPU was over the agent's last 2s sample, every core
counted: 100 is all of them. `None` until it has two samples.
Defaulted the same way.

running.description:
PipeWire answered. When it did not, `error` says why and the sides
carry only the settings.

setting.description: audio.output or audio.input, as set or defaulted.

using.description: The device in use, if any.

fallback.description: Why that is not what the setting names: `usb is not connected`.

muted.description: Muted: audio.mute, or the setting is `off`.

AudioSide.description: The output side or the input side.

name.description: What audio.output or audio.input takes to pick exactly this one.

available.description:
Something is plugged in, as far as the hardware can tell; `None` when
it cannot.

in_use.description: The one the settings put in use.

needs_profile.description:
Not there until its sound card is switched to another profile, which
choosing it does.

AudioDevice.description: One output or input as PipeWire has it.

FsUsage.description:
How full one mounted filesystem is, in bytes. `available` is what a
process that is not root can still write.

script_problem.description: Why the script is not in the page, when it is not.

synchronized.description: timedated's `NTPSynchronized`: the kernel clock is disciplined.

TimeSummary.description: The clock in one line, for `device status`.

model.description: `ThinkCentre M720q`, `Raspberry Pi 3 Model B Plus Rev 1.3`.

board.description: The mainboard, or on the Pi the manufacturer that built it.

firmware.description: The BIOS version and date. The Pi does not say.

cpu.description: `Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-8500T CPU @ 2.10GHz`, or the Pi's SoC, `BCM2837`.

Hardware.description:
What the hardware says it is, from DMI on x86 or the device tree on the
Pi (docs/hardware.md). `None` is "the firmware does not say".

MemUsage.description:
RAM, in bytes, from `/proc/meminfo`. `available` is `MemAvailable`: what
can be handed out without swapping, page cache included.

addresses.description: Global IPv4 addresses, with the interface each is on.

online.description:
Whether the last public address lookup answered; `None` until one
has been tried.

setup.description: While the hotspot is up and the device unclaimed.

WelcomeInfo.description: What the welcome page shows, the body of `welcome.json` too.

qr.description: An SVG QR code that joins a phone to the hotspot.

url.description: Where Quick Setup is on the hotspot.

unit.description: Only this unit, or a pattern of them (`tessaro-schedule-*`).

lines.description: The last this many entries, 100 by default. Ignored with `cursor`.

cursor.description: Only what came after this, from the last page's `cursor`.

entries.description:
journalctl's JSON entries, oldest first: `MESSAGE`,
`SYSLOG_IDENTIFIER`, `PRIORITY`, `__REALTIME_TIMESTAMP` and the rest.

cursor.description:
Where the next page starts: send it back as `cursor` to get only
what came after. The one sent when nothing new came, `None` for an
empty journal.

__REALTIME_TIMESTAMP.description: Microseconds since the epoch, as a string.

JournalEntry.description:
One journal entry as journalctl writes it: the fields a client reads,
and whatever else the entry has. Only described, for the API's
document: the entries pass through as they are.

JournalText.description: A journal field: text, or its bytes when it is not UTF-8.

hotspot.description:
The hotspot's new password, shown once like the root password. `None`
on a device without its WiFi interface, or an older one.

issued_by.description: The id of the token that issued it, `claim`, or `local`.

password.description: Generated, and answered once, without it.
The generated password, when the server chose it. Shown once.

fresh.description: Unclaimed and nothing set yet: Webconfig opens on Quick Setup.

token.description: The token the request came in with, directly or through a session.

timeout.description:
How long a browser session lasts without use, in seconds
(`access.session_timeout`).

WebSession.description:
Who a browser is to the device: what Webconfig asks first
(docs/webconfig.md).

oneOf.description: No credential: the device is unclaimed, or the endpoint is public.
An `Authorization: Bearer` token.
A browser session's cookie.
The local socket.

Via.description: How a request was let in.

expires_in.description: Seconds it can still be redeemed in.

Ticket.description:
A one-time ticket that signs a browser in: `tessaro-ctl access
webconfig` puts it in the address it opens.

fingerprint.description: SHA256 fingerprint of the key sent.

added.description: False when the key was already there.

host_keys.description:
The device's host keys, as OpenSSH `TYPE BASE64` lines. Empty when
the device could not read them; the client then falls back to
ssh's own first-use prompt.

key.description:
Its `SHA256:` fingerprint, a unique prefix of it, or its exact
comment.

fingerprint.description:
The removed key's SHA256 fingerprint. `None` from an older device,
which only says it in `message`.

SshKeyRevoked.description: What `ssh-key-revoke` removed. `message` is what an older client prints.

values.description: What a value may be, in words.

default.description: The image's default, if it has one.

value.description: What this device has set, if anything.

input.description: The control an editor offers for it. Defaulted for older devices.

oneOf.description:
Read by tessaro-agent at start: the agent restarts itself. Invisible
on screen - the browser is left alone.
Read by tessaro-kiosk.service: the browser restarts.

Read by tessaro-weston-config before the compositor starts: Weston
restarts, and with it (`PartOf=`) the browser and the agent.

The device's own NetworkManager profiles: applied as one network
change the device verifies and rolls back by itself, before the
setting is saved at all. Nothing restarts.

PipeWire, through WirePlumber: the agent switches the output, the
input and their volumes on the running sound server at once. Nothing
restarts, and a sound that is playing moves over.

The Raspberry Pi firmware, through `tessaro.txt` on the boot
partition, which it reads only when the board powers on. Nothing
restarts: the change takes effect at the next reboot.

The system clock, through systemd-timedated and systemd-timesyncd:
the agent sets the timezone and the NTP servers on the running
system. Only systemd-timesyncd restarts, and only when its servers
change; the browser follows `/etc/localtime` by itself.

The device's local forwarding proxy, `tessaro-proxy.service`: its
config in `/run` is rendered again, and the unit restarts, or stops
when network.proxy.url is empty. The browser restarts only when the
proxy is switched on or off, which changes its policy.

Consumer.description: What has to happen for a changed value to take effect.

oneOf.description: A checkbox: `1` or `0`.
One of these.
A whole number in a range.
Text.
Nothing to enter: the device reports it.

KeyInput.description: How a value is entered. `config set` checks what is entered either way.

key.description: One key; all of them without it.

oneOf.description: The image's default, from /usr/lib/tessaro-kiosk/tessaro-kiosk.env.
Set on this device.
Read-only: reported by the device as it is right now.

if_revision.description: Refuse unless the settings are still at this revision.

apply.description:
Restart what reads the keys. Without it the change waits for the next
restart.

verify.description: What the device checks before it keeps a change to network keys.

oneOf.description: The default gateway answers a ping.
This host answers a ping.
A TCP connection to this host and port opens.
Only the route and the activation.

Verify.description:
What the device checks, on its own, before it keeps a network change.
Whatever it is, the change must also leave the device with a default
route if it had one, and a connection it activated must come up.

restarted.description: Units restarted, or to be restarted once this reply is out.

network.description:
What the network change did, when network keys changed: its checks.
A rolled-back change is an error, not an `Applied`. Defaulted for
older devices.

audio.description:
What the audio.* keys did on the sound server, in words, when they
changed: where sound now plays and how loud, or why it could not be
applied (the setting is saved either way).

time.description:
What the time.* keys did to the clock, in words, when they changed
(the setting is saved either way). Defaulted for older devices.

reboot.description:
A setting the firmware reads at power-on changed on disk, so it takes
effect at the next reboot, which the device leaves to the operator.
Defaulted for older devices.

note.description: Anything the operator should know about a kept change.

NetChange.description:
What a network change did. Kept on the device as the last one, so a
client whose connection went with the change can still ask.

ScreenPower.description: Whether the display is on, as the compositor has it.

selector.description: The field to focus when showing; the one with the focus without it.

await_promise.description: Wait for a returned Promise and answer with what it settles to.

user_gesture.description: Run as if the user had just touched the page.

value.description:
`None` for `undefined`, and for a value JSON cannot hold (a
function, a DOM node): `description` says what it was.

kind.description: The value's type as JavaScript names it, `undefined` included.

EvalResult.description: What `eval` came to: the value, as JSON, or what it threw.

position.description: From 1, the highest priority: it wins a policy others set too.

problem.description:
Why the stored text no longer passes the check, when it does not: the
device leaves such a document out of the policy.

PolicyDoc.description: One stored document with its text, as typed.

text.description:
The document as typed: one JSON object of Chromium policies, `//`
and `/* */` comments and trailing commas allowed. At most
`POLICY_TEXT_MAX` bytes.

if_revision.description:
Refuse unless the stored document is still at this revision; `""`
refuses unless there is none yet. Unconditional without it.

position.description:
Where it goes in the priority order, from 1, the highest. A new one
goes to the bottom without it; a stored one stays where it is.

unchanged.description: The stored text and position were already these; nothing was written.

overrides_image.description: Keys it sets that the image sets too: its value wins.

shadows.description: Keys a document lower in priority sets too, which this one wins.

shadowed_by.description: Keys a document higher in priority sets too, which win over this one.

restarted.description: The browser was restarted to read the new policy.

PolicyOverlap.description: A key set in more than one place, and the document on the other side.

position.description: From 1, the highest priority; past the last, the last.

Where it is now: what was asked, held to 1 and the number of
documents.

EffectiveEntry.description: One entry of the policy Chromium reads.

oneOf.description: The image's own policy.
A stored document.
The device, from its settings (`managed`).

PolicySource.description: Where one entry of the merged policy comes from.

interface.description: The interface with the IPv4 default route.

dns.description: The upstream servers, not systemd-resolved's 127.0.0.53 stub.

public_ip.description:
The address the internet sees, as the agent last found it through
Cloudflare's trace; `None` until it has. Defaulted for older devices.

proxy.description:
network.proxy.url with its password masked; `None` without a proxy.
Defaulted for older devices.

carrier.description: A cable or an association, if the driver says.

kind.description:
`ethernet`, `wifi`, or NetworkManager's own type name for anything
else.

device.description: The device it is active on, or bound to.

saved.description:
Written to disk. A profile under `/run` counts as unsaved, the
managed ones included.

managed.description:
One of the fixed profiles the agent renders from settings on
every boot, so unsaved but never lost.

NetProfile.description: A NetworkManager profile, as `net profiles` lists it.

addresses.description: What its device has right now, from the kernel. Empty when inactive.

enabled.description: The radio, as software (`net wifi on|off`) left it.

hardware_enabled.description: A hardware kill switch, if the device has one.

fallback.description:
The client network the hotspot stands in for, when the client did not
connect after boot (`network.wifi.fallback_after`). Until the next boot.

rescan.description: Scan first. Without it, what the device last saw.

known.description: A saved profile has this SSID.

psk.description: Without it the stored one: rejoining the same network.

security.description: Found by scanning when not given; a hidden network needs it.

Secret.description:
A secret on its way to the device: a WiFi password. It serializes as the
plain string, but prints as `***`, so a `{:?}` of a command - in a log
line, a panic, a test failure - never shows it.

oneOf.description: WPA2 personal.
WPA3 personal.

JobStarted.description: A job the device started: poll it at `/api/v1/jobs/{job}`.

direct.description: Go around network.proxy.url, straight to Cloudflare.

url.description: network.proxy.url with its password masked; `None` without a proxy.

listen.description: Where the device's local proxy listens, `127.0.0.1:3128`.

ip.description: The address the internet sees through the proxy.

error.description: Why it could not be reached, when it could not.

ProxyTested.description: What `network proxy test` got through the proxy.

fingerprint.description: SHA-256 of the DER, lower-case hex.

not_after.description: When it expires, seconds since the epoch, UTC.

self_signed.description: Signed by its own key: a root rather than an intermediate.

CertInfo.description: One extra certificate authority the device trusts.

present.description: Already trusted; nothing changed for these.

CertsAdded.description: What `net-cert-add` did with each certificate it was sent.

cert.description: Its SHA-256 fingerprint, a unique prefix of it, or its exact subject.

unallocated.description:
Space after the last partition that `storage-grow` would give to
`/data`; 0 when there is too little to bother (`GROW_MIN`).

fstype.description: Only for filesystems that are mounted.

Partition.description:
One partition of the disk the device runs from. Sizes and offsets in
bytes.

input.description: Record from the input instead of playing a tone.

peak_dbfs.description:
The recording's loudest sample and its average, dBFS: 0 is full
scale, silence is far below -60.

saved.description:
Where the recording was left in the file store, for `tessaro-ctl
files download` or `http://127.0.0.1/files/`.

error.description: Why timedated or timesyncd could not be read, if one of them could not.

setting_servers.description: time.ntp.servers as set: empty uses DHCP's, then the fallback.

now_usec.description: The system clock, microseconds since the epoch.

local_time.description: The same, as a wall clock in `timezone`: `2026-09-25 14:03:12`.

zone_abbreviation.description: `CEST`, and its distance from UTC in seconds east.

rtc_usec.description: The hardware clock, where there is one; a Raspberry Pi has none.

local_rtc.description: The hardware clock keeps local time instead of UTC.

synchronized.description: The kernel clock is disciplined by NTP.

server_name.description: The server timesyncd uses now, by name and address.

poll_interval_usec.description: How often timesyncd asks, and between what bounds it moves.

root_distance_max_usec.description: A server farther than this from a reference clock is not trusted.

frequency.description:
The kernel's frequency correction - how fast this clock drifts - in
units of 2^-16 ppm, as adjtimex keeps it. `frequency_ppm` reads it.

last.description: The last NTP answer, if there was one.

TimeStatus.description:
Everything systemd says about the clock. Every field is what timedated
or timesyncd reported, never measured by the agent; `None` is "not
reported", which a service that is down or has not synced yet does.

leap.description:
0 no warning, 1 or 2 a leap second at the end of the day, 3 the
server is not synchronized.

stratum.description: The server's distance from a reference clock: 1 is attached to one.

precision.description: The server clock's precision, log2 seconds (-20 is about 1 µs).

reference.description:
The server's reference: a clock name like `GPS` at stratum 1, else
the address of its own server.

offset_usec.description: How far this clock was from the server's: positive is behind.

delay_usec.description: The round trip, less the time the server took to answer.

jitter_usec.description: timesyncd's running estimate of how much the offset varies.

spike.description: The last answer was thrown away as an outlier.

received_usec.description: When the answer arrived, microseconds since the epoch.

NtpSample.description:
timesyncd's `NTPMessage`: the last answer from the server, and what
follows from its timestamps.

runtime.description:
Set at runtime by the agent: the DHCP servers, while time.ntp.servers
is empty.

system.description: time.ntp.servers, from the agent's timesyncd drop-in.

link.description: Per-link servers, which only systemd-networkd hands out; empty here.

fallback.description: The image's fallback, used when none of the above has any.

dhcp.description: What the network's DHCP offered, whether in use or not.

NtpServers.description: Where timesyncd's servers come from, in the order it tries them.

id.description: Stable across renames; names the schedule's systemd units.

calendar.description:
systemd `OnCalendar` expressions; the schedule fires when any of
them does.

lines.description: Shell command lines, each run with `/bin/sh -c` as root, in order.

timeout_s.description: The longest a whole run may take before systemd kills it.

next.description: When the timer fires next; `None` while disabled.

running.description: Runs going right now; they may overlap.

units.description: The journal pattern of its runs, for `logs --unit`.

ScheduleInfo.description: One schedule and what systemd reports about it.

oneOf.description: The run ends there, failed.
The next line runs anyway.

OnError.description: What a run does when one of its lines fails.

Moment.description: A moment as the device reports it.

status.description:
systemd's `$EXIT_STATUS` of the last line that ran: an exit code
or a signal name.

calendar.description:
systemd `OnCalendar` expressions; the schedule fires when any of
them does.

lines.description: Shell command lines, each run with `/bin/sh -c` as root, in order.

timeout_s.description: The longest a whole run may take before systemd kills it.

ScheduleSpec.description: What a schedule is: when it fires and what a run does.

ScheduleChange.description:
What is given replaces what the schedule has; a given `calendar` or
`lines` replaces the whole list.

count.description: How many run times to answer with.

normalized.description: Each expression as systemd normalizes it, in the order sent.

next.description: The next times any of them fires, earliest first.

enabled.description:
printer.enable: `window.print()` and the page bridge print. The
device's own clients print either way.

PrinterList.description: Every printer, and whether pages may print.

name.description:
`[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*`, unique on the device: what a page and
`tessaro-ctl printer print` name it by.

uri.description:
Where it is, as CUPS spells it: `ipp://host/ipp/print`,
`ipps://...`, `socket://host:9100`, `usb://...`, or a `dnssd://` URI
from `printer-discover`.

media.description:
The paper a job gets when it names none, as the printer names it:
`iso_a4_210x297mm`, `na_letter_8.5x11in`, `A4`. Empty for the
printer's own default.

default.description: `window.print()` prints here.

state.description:
`idle`, `printing`, `stopped`, or `missing` while CUPS does not have
it yet: it did not answer when it was set up, and the device keeps
trying.

message.description:
Why, as CUPS says: `offline-report`, `media-empty`, or the error that
kept it from being set up.

markers.description: Only from `printer-show`, and only from a printer that reports them.

model.description: The make and model the printer gave, for a driverless one.

PrinterInfo.description: One printer and what CUPS reports about it.

oneOf.description:
Driverless: IPP Everywhere or AirPrint. CUPS asks the printer what
it takes and turns a PDF into it.

The bytes go to the printer as they are: a receipt printer's ESC/POS,
a label printer's ZPL, or a document already in the printer's
language.

level.description: Percent left, when the printer says.

PrinterMarker.description: One supply a printer reports: an ink, a toner, a waste box.

name.description:
`[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*`, unique on the device: what a page and
`tessaro-ctl printer print` name it by.

uri.description:
Where it is, as CUPS spells it: `ipp://host/ipp/print`,
`ipps://...`, `socket://host:9100`, `usb://...`, or a `dnssd://` URI
from `printer-discover`.

media.description:
The paper a job gets when it names none, as the printer names it:
`iso_a4_210x297mm`, `na_letter_8.5x11in`, `A4`. Empty for the
printer's own default.

PrinterSpec.description: What a printer is: how it is reached and how it is driven.

path.description:
A file in the store, from its root, for a document sent with no
body: one larger than `PRINT_DATA_MAX`.

media.description:
The paper, as the printer names it; the printer's own `media` when
not given.

PrintQuery.description:
Where a document goes and how. Without a body, `path` names a file in
the store to print instead.

submitted.description: When it was sent, as CUPS writes it.

name.description: The file being uploaded or staged.

verified.description:
Bytes of the upload checked against its SHA-256, of `size`: the first
step of preparing, skipped with `verify: false`. Defaulted for older
devices, which do not report it.

prepared.description: Mapped bytes of the image checked, of `to_prepare`.

repartition.description:
The whole disk is rewritten, not the root partition. Defaulted for
older devices, which cannot.

last.description: What the last boot that applied an update did.

oneOf.description: Nothing under way.
Part of the image has arrived.

All of it has; the device is checking the whole file against its
SHA-256 (`verified` of `size`). Skipped with `verify: false`.

Checked; the device is decompressing it once as a dry run, checking
each bmap range it will write (`prepared` of `to_prepare`).
Staged and verified; waiting for `update-commit`.
Committed; applied at the next boot.
Preparing failed; `error` says why. Begin again to retry.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the whole file, lower-case hex.

verify.description:
Check the whole upload against `sha256` before preparing it.
The bmap's per-range checksums are checked either way.

repartition.description:
Write the whole disk (partition table, every partition, `/data`)
instead of the root partition: for a device on another disk
layout. Implies wiping `/data`; a power cut while it writes needs
a physical reflash. An older device ignores it and refuses the
layout as before.

ImageUpload.description:
The image `update-begin` describes. Its fields sit in the command itself
on the wire, next to `cmd`.

offset.description: Bytes the device already has. Send from here.
Where this piece starts: what the device said it has.

Received.description:
How much of an upload - an image, or one file - the device has, after a
chunk.

wipe_data.description: Re-create `/data` too: settings, the claim, the browser profile.

path.description: From the store's root; the root itself when empty.

entries.description:
Names sorted; recursively, depth first, a directory before what is
in it. Paths are always from the store's root.

path.description: From the root of the store, `/`-separated.

mtime.description:
Modification time, whole seconds since the epoch. What `sync`
compares, with the size.
Seconds since the epoch, stamped on the file once it is complete.

offset.description: Bytes the device already has of this file. Send from here.

after.description: The first step to answer with: the last page's `next`.

events.description:
Its steps from number `after` on, in order: `PingEvent`s,
`SpeedtestEvent`s, `StorageGrowEvent`s or `PrinterFound`s, by the
job.

done.description: It has ended. With `error`, it failed.

JobEvent.description:
One step of a job, of the kind the job is. Only described, for the
API's document.

oneOf.description: The address the host resolved to.

PingEvent.description: One step of `net-ping`, in the order they arrive.

colo.description: The Cloudflare data centre answering, as an airport code.

oneOf.description: Where Cloudflare sees the device from.
Round trips of an empty request, less the server's own time.
Every sample of one payload size in one direction.

The median at the largest size that produced samples: small payloads
never leave slow start and under-report a fast link.

SpeedtestEvent.description: One step of `speedtest`, in the order they arrive.

oneOf.description:
What would change. Equal sizes mean that part is already done; both
equal, that there is nothing to grow.
About to run `command`.
The sizes afterwards, read back from the kernel and the filesystem.

StorageGrowEvent.description: One step of `storage-grow`, in the order they arrive. Sizes in bytes.

description.description: What the printer calls itself, or its make and model.

kind.description:
How it is best driven: `ipp` for a printer that answers IPP, `raw`
for a socket or USB one.

known.description: A printer the device has already, by this URI.

PrinterFound.description: One step of `printer-discover`: a printer CUPS found.

session.name: __Host-tessaro-{node id}
session.description: Set by signing in (`access/session`, `access/ticket/redeem`) or claiming from a browser. Browser requests must come from the device's own origin.
